threads.body: Using `@TestMethodOrder(OrderAnnotation.class)` + `@Order` introduces ordering requirements across the entire test class (and all subclasses). Since this test already recreates the client in `@BeforeEach`, ordering shouldn’t be needed; keeping tests order-independent helps avoid hidden coupling/flakiness. Consider removing the method ordering unless there’s a concrete dependency that can’t be eliminated.

`setConnectionMinimumIdleSize(0)` is applied in the shared `@BeforeEach` setup, so it changes behavior for *all* tests in this class (including existing ones). That can unintentionally alter coverage and can increase flakiness/latency by forcing more reconnects. Consider scoping this setting only to the lazy-connection regression test (e.g., by building a dedicated `RedissonClient` inside that test or using `TestInfo` in `@BeforeEach` to conditionally apply the config).

This regression test is meant to validate context propagation under the `parent` span, but the `SET` span assertion doesn’t currently verify parentage. Adding `.hasParent(trace.getSpan(0))` here would make the test directly assert the intended behavior (no lost context).
Similarly, the `GET` span assertion should verify it remains a child of the `parent` span (e.g., `.hasParent(trace.getSpan(0))`) to directly test that context isn’t lost across command execution.

threads.body: `setConnectionMinimumIdleSize(0)` is set for every test via `@BeforeEach`, which changes behavior for the entire suite (including existing tests like `futureWhenComplete`). Consider scoping this configuration only to the lazy-connection regression scenario so the rest of the tests continue exercising the default pooling behavior.

Introducing `@TestMethodOrder(OrderAnnotation.class)` and `@Order` makes the test suite order-dependent. Given the client is recreated in `@BeforeEach`, test ordering shouldn’t be necessary; consider removing ordering to keep the suite resilient and easier to maintain.

`futureWhenCompleteLazyConnection()` is currently effectively identical to the existing `futureWhenComplete()` test (same body and assertions). With the global `connectionMinimumIdleSize(0)` change, both tests now exercise the same configuration. Consider either (a) making only this test use the “lazy connection” config, keeping `futureWhenComplete()` as the baseline case, or (b) removing one of the duplicates to avoid redundant coverage/time.
